oneLine: The network's front door for vendors: issues purchase orders to vendor-run nodes and takes their answers, labels, shipments, stock feeds and inbound receipts.

rows.title: Onboard a vendor
rows.story: A partner manager creates a vendor account and sets how long the vendor has to acknowledge each purchase order. Onboarding the same vendor again returns the existing account.

rows.title: Suspend a vendor
rows.story: A partner manager suspends a vendor. While suspended, every write the vendor sends is refused.

rows.title: Reinstate a vendor
rows.story: A partner manager lifts the suspension and the vendor can write again.

rows.title: Issue a purchase order
rows.story: When a group is released to a vendor-run node, one purchase order is issued to that node's vendor. It names the stock owner of every line and the time by which the vendor must answer.
rows.policy: Whenever a group is released to a vendor-run node, issue one purchase order for it

then.does: tracks the order for the node's scorecard

rows.title: Acknowledge a purchase order
rows.story: The vendor's system polls its orders, then accepts or rejects the whole order in one call. It must cover every line and answer before the deadline. The call returns a transaction id, not the result.

rows.title: Settle the vendor's queued writes
rows.story: A processor runs each queued vendor write once it is due and records the outcome. A successful acknowledgement becomes an accepted or rejected order, a successful shipment confirmation a shipped one.
rows.policy: Whenever a queued vendor write is due, run it and apply its outcome to the purchase order

then.does: locks the group on acceptance, tries another node on rejection, marks it shipped
records a shipment-confirmed scan for each tracking number
counts the answer and the shipment for the node's scorecard

rows.title: Expire an order nobody answered
rows.story: A sweep finds issued orders past their acknowledge-by time. They expire so order-sourcing can try another node.
rows.policy: Every sweep, an issued order past its acknowledge-by time expires

then.does: excludes the node and searches again
counts the missed deadline for the node's scorecard

rows.title: Cancel an order when sourcing cancels
rows.story: When order-sourcing cancels a group, its purchase order is cancelled, but only while it still waits for the vendor's answer. After the vendor answered, the order stays and the refusal is only logged.
rows.policy: Whenever a group is cancelled, cancel its purchase order if it is still waiting for an answer

rows.title: Cancel an order when a release is withdrawn
rows.story: When order-sourcing withdraws a merged release, the purchase order of exactly that release is cancelled, never a newer one for the same group.
rows.policy: Whenever a release is withdrawn, cancel the purchase order of that release if it is still waiting

rows.title: Request shipping labels
rows.story: For an accepted order the vendor asks for one label per package. This is the one write answered at once: one label is issued per package by shipping-and-tracking, and labels already issued are returned again.

then.does: is called right away to issue one label per package

rows.title: Confirm a shipment
rows.story: The vendor confirms that an accepted order shipped. The tracking numbers must be exactly the ones of the labels issued; the confirmation is queued and settled later.

rows.title: Register a node or send its stock
rows.story: The vendor registers a node, declares its operating profile or sends an inventory feed. Each write is queued and settled later; node-topology and offer-availability do the real work and the answer carries the new node id.

rows.title: Report what the dock received
rows.story: The vendor reports cartons received for an inbound shipment. The report is checked against the shipment's manifest; counting more or fewer units than listed is reported, never refused.

then.does: records the findings and closes the inbound shipment
uses the carton findings for the node's inbound accuracy score

rows.title: Keep the inbound shipments copy
rows.story: Seller-inbound announces shipments with their carton manifests. A copy lets the vendor poll what is on its way and lets receipts be checked without a live call.
rows.policy: Whenever an inbound shipment is labelled, shipped or received, update the local shipments copy

rows.title: Keep the vendor node list
rows.story: Node-topology announces nodes, profiles and status changes. A copy tells which nodes belong to which vendor and each node's handling time, used to set the answer deadline.
rows.policy: Whenever a node is registered, profiled, activated, suspended or retired, update the local node list

rows.title: Keep the listings and packaging copy
rows.story: Offer-availability announces listings and the pack levels of each catalogue item. Listings let stock feeds be checked; pack levels appear on purchase order lines.
rows.policy: Whenever a listing is created, keep it so a stock feed can be checked against its node

hotspots.text: A cancel that arrives after the vendor answered is refused and only logged: nobody is told, and the vendor may still ship.
The vendor's identity is a request field, not authentication. The ownership check only keeps a vendor away from other vendors' nodes inside the cluster.
A withdrawn release can be accepted in the one message hop before the cancel arrives: the vendor then holds an order for the old merged lines.
A receipt is judged when it is sent, not again when processed, so two receipts for one shipment can both be accepted.
The vendor-account events (onboarded, suspended, reinstated) have no consumer that acts on them yet.
